segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Good morning Mrs. Santos. We are reviewing your blood pressure today. How have you been feeling since our last visit?

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: Good morning Doc. Generally okay, but I get occasional mild occipital headaches in the afternoon when I am tired from work.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Are you experiencing any chest discomfort, palpitations, shortness of breath, or swelling in your feet?

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: No chest pain at all. No difficulty breathing and no ankle swelling. None of those.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Good. And what medications are you currently taking, exactly as prescribed?

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I take Amlodipine 5 milligrams once daily in the morning. To be honest, I sometimes miss the Sunday dose when we visit our grandchildren. My sister takes Losartan 50mg, but I do not take that.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Understood. Any drug allergies that we should know about?

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: Penicillin gives me an itchy skin rash and hives. No other allergies.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Let me take your blood pressure right now in the right arm sitting. It is 138 over 86 millimeters of mercury, pulse rate 74 regular.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: Your blood pressure is borderline elevated today, likely related to missed doses. We will keep Amlodipine at 5mg daily. Please set a phone alarm so you don't miss Sunday doses. Return in 4 weeks for repeat BP check, or sooner if headaches worsen.
